chunks.title: Tokenised stocks, priced two ways
chunks.text: The Gully Labs tracker checks every tokenised stock on Robinhood Chain and BNB Chain against its fair price, live. These docs cover how it works, the public API it is built on, and the widget that puts it on your own page. Docs for the Gully Labs stock token tracker: how its fair and onchain prices are read, the public API, the embeddable widget and API keys.

chunks.title: Tokenised stocks, priced two ways
chunks.text: For each stock token the tracker reads two prices: the fair price, from the Chainlink feed for that stock, read on chain; and the onchain price, what the token trades at in its deepest pool. The difference, as a percentage of fair, is the gap. A token trading above its fair price is at a premium; below it, at a discount. The live page is at gullylabs.xyz/tracker. Everything it shows comes from the same public API these docs describe.

chunks.text: The public API as your browser sees it right now, checked every 15 seconds, and the widest gaps the tracker stands behind at this moment.

chunks.title: Tokenised stocks, priced two ways
chunks.text: Fair prices are Chainlink feeds read on chain with latestRoundData(). Onchain prices are read from each token’s deepest pool on chain; DexScreener and GeckoTerminal only find the pool. Nothing is estimated or typed in: a price that cannot be read is reported as unreadable, never as zero. The methodology gives the exact rules. The tracker reports what two public sources say. It is not investment advice, and a gap is not a promise that anyone can trade it away.

chunks.title: Tracker methodology
chunks.text: How each number is read, how the gap is computed, and the rules that keep a small pool or a closed market from making a headline. How the Gully Labs tracker reads a stock token's fair price from Chainlink and its onchain price from the deepest pool, and the rules that decide when a gap is flagged.

chunks.title: Tracker methodology
chunks.text: For every token in the tracker’s feed table, on every chain it covers, two numbers are read live on each refresh: Fair: the Chainlink feed for that stock, read on chain. Onchain: the token’s price in its deepest pool, read straight from that pool’s contract. Both are in US dollars per token. Each is either a number or unreadable; an unreadable price is never replaced with zero or with an older figure.

chunks.title: Tracker methodology
chunks.text: Every feed is read with latestRoundData() in one batched call per chain. A round whose answer is zero or negative, or whose update time is zero, counts as unreadable. The answer is scaled by the feed’s decimals. Robinhood Chain The feeds price the token itself (feedPrices: "tokenized-instrument"), so fair is the feed’s answer. BNB Chain The feeds price the underlying share (feedPrices: "underlying-share"). One raw bStock token is a number of shares given by the token’s own uiMultiplier() (ERC-8056, where 1e18 means 1.0). The multiplier is read on chain on every refresh, because the issuer changes it at a split. If the multiplier cannot be read, or reads as zero, the fair price is unreadable for that token. The multiplier used is returned in each row as multiplier.

chunks.title: Tracker methodology
chunks.text: Once an hour the tracker asks DexScreener (GeckoTerminal if DexScreener refuses) for every pool of every token, 30 tokens per request. For each token it keeps the pools with a positive price and picks one: pools quoted against a native coin or a dollar stablecoin come first (WETH, ETH, WBNB, BNB, USDC, USDG, USDT, USD1, FDUSD), then the deepest by liquidity. Between those reads, every refresh prices the chosen pool from the chain itself: slot0() on a v3 pool, StateView.getSlot0 on a Uniswap v4 pool. The pool’s ratio is turned into dollars with $1 for a dollar stablecoin, Chainlink’s ETH/USD or BNB/USD feed for the native coin, and this cycle’s fair price where the quote is itself a stock token. The chain’s poolSource says on chain when this is the source. The row’s pool object names the pool used, its liquidity and 24-hour volume, and totals across every pool found for the token. Liquidity and volume come from the hourly read, because the chain does not publish them in a usable form.

chunks.title: Tracker methodology
chunks.text: Every row carries a status, decided in this order: feed-unreadable (fair is null): The Chainlink feed (or, on BNB Chain, the multiplier) could not be read. pool-unreadable (pool read failed): DexScreener could not be read for this chain. no-pool (onchain is null): No pool with a usable price was found. unverified (onchain ≥ 5× or ≤ 1/5 of fair; or |gap| ≥ 15% unless the pool holds $1,000,000+ and was read on chain this cycle): The figure is implausible for a tokenised stock: far more often a bad print (a misread venue, an old API reading, a decimals slip) than a price. gapPct is withheld (null), the figure stays in rawGapPct, and untrustedReason says why. Never flagged, ranked, alerted on or recorded in the history. thin (liquidity < $10,000): The chosen pool is too small to trust. Shown, never flagged. in-line (|gap| < 1%): Within the noise. Robinhood Chain feeds only move on a 0.5% deviation. drifting (1% ≤ |gap| < 2%): Moving away from fair, not yet flagged. premium (gap ≥ 2%): Flagged: trading above fair. discount (gap ≤ −2%): Flagged: trading below fair. The thresholds are returned with every response in rules (minLiquidityUsd, inLinePct, flagPct, implausiblePct, trustLiquidityUsd, unitsRatio), so a client never has to hard-code them. Trust and provenance

chunks.title: Tracker methodology
chunks.text: Flagged: trading below fair. The thresholds are returned with every response in rules (minLiquidityUsd, inLinePct, flagPct, implausiblePct, trustLiquidityUsd, unitsRatio), so a client never has to hard-code them. Trust and provenance Every row says whether the tracker stands behind its gap. trusted is true only for premium, discount, drifting and in-line rows whose pool read is fresh; otherwise untrustedReason gives the reason in a sentence (a thin pool, an implausible figure, an unreadable source, or a pool read served from the last good one while sources back off). Top movers and gap alerts only ever use trusted rows; the five-minute history skips every row without a gap (an unverified row included) and every stale pool read. onchainSource says where this cycle’s onchain price came from: chain when the pool contract was read directly, api when it is the price API’s reading for a venue that cannot be re-read on chain. onchainAt is when that price was read, so an API reading shows its own age.

chunks.title: Tracker methodology
chunks.text: Stock feeds follow market hours. Each chain reports whether its session is open now: Robinhood Chain, 24/5: Chainlink’s US equities 24/5 session, Sunday 20:00 to Friday 20:00, New York time. BNB Chain, NYSE hours: 09:30 to 16:00 New York time, Monday to Friday. Outside its session a feed holds its last value, so the gap is measured against the last session’s close, not presented as a live mispricing. Market holidays are not modelled: on a holiday the session reads as open and the feed’s update time, returned as feedUpdatedAt, shows how old the fair price is.

chunks.title: Tracker methodology
chunks.text: The tracker reads its sources at most once every two minutes. Every visitor and every API caller share that one read. If the chain cannot be read and neither API answers, that chain backs off (one minute, doubling, at most 30 minutes) and keeps serving its last good pool read, marked poolsStale: true with its time in poolsAsOf, and poolStale: true on each row. A pool read older than six hours is dropped rather than shown. Fair prices stay live throughout. Every five minutes one snapshot per token is recorded, and kept for seven days. Rows without a gap, or with a stale pool read, are not recorded. The history endpoint serves them.

chunks.title: Tracker methodology
chunks.text: The onchain price is one pool’s price as DexScreener reports it, not a volume-weighted average across venues. Liquidity figures are DexScreener’s, in US dollars. Only tokens in the tracker’s verified feed tables are covered; a stock token without a Chainlink feed on its chain does not appear. A gap may not be tradable: pool depth, fees, slippage and issuer rules all stand between a gap and a profit. The tracker reports what Chainlink and the pools say, with the rules above. It is not investment advice and makes no promise about any token.

chunks.title: API reference
chunks.text: Three read-only JSON endpoints. No key is needed to start; a key raises your rate limit. The Gully Labs tracker API: GET /api/tracker, GET /api/tracker/history and GET /api/tracker/movers, every response field, caching, CORS, rate limits, API keys and errors, with a real example response.

chunks.title: API reference
chunks.text: Base URL (https://gullylabs.xyz): Every endpoint lives under /api/tracker. Methods (GET, OPTIONS): Anything else answers 405. Format (JSON): UTF-8. Times are ISO 8601 in UTC, except history points, which use Unix seconds. CORS (Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *): Call it from any browser origin. Preflight allows the Authorization and Content-Type headers. Auth (Optional): Send Authorization: Bearer <key> for a higher limit. See API keys. Prices are US dollars per token. Any price may be null, meaning it could not be read; it is never replaced with zero. Live, from your browser: the response time of /api/tracker, measured every 10 seconds while this tab is open, and the rows it returns by status.

chunks.title: API reference
chunks.text: The whole tracker: every chain, the rules, the sources and one row per token. Top level generatedAt (string (ISO)): When this answer was built. chains (Chain[]): One entry per chain, below. rules (object): The thresholds in force: minLiquidityUsd (pools below are “thin”), inLinePct (gaps below are “in line”), flagPct (gaps at or above are flagged), implausiblePct (a gap this wide needs a deep pool read on chain to be believed), trustLiquidityUsd (how deep that pool must be) and unitsRatio (an onchain price this many times fair, or this fraction of it, is a units error). sources (object): fair and onchain describe the two price sources; tables names the feed table used per chain. rows (Row[]): One per token. See Rows. chains[] key (string): Chain key used everywhere else: robinhood or bsc. id (number): EVM chain id (4663, 56). name (string): Display name. sessionOpen (boolean): Whether the chain’s feed session is open now. See sessions. sessionName (string): 24/5 or NYSE hours. fairMethod (string): How fair is derived on this chain, in words. poolsAsOf (string | null): Time of the pool read in use. poolsStale (boolean): True when the pool read is the last good one, served while every price source for that chain is backing off. poolSource (string | null): Where pool prices came from this cycle: on chain, DexScreener or GeckoTerminal.

chunks.title: API reference
chunks.text: chain (string): Chain key. ticker (string): Stock ticker, e.g. NVDA. name (string): Company name. token (string): Token contract address. feed (string): Chainlink feed address. fair (number | null): Fair price in USD per token. feedPrices (string): tokenized-instrument (the feed prices the token) or underlying-share (it prices the share). multiplier (number | null): Shares per token from uiMultiplier() on BNB Chain; 1 on Robinhood Chain; null when the feed could not be read. feedUpdatedAt (string | null): When the feed last updated. feedError (string | null): Why the feed could not be read, if it could not. onchain (number | null): Price in the chosen pool, USD per token. gapPct (number | null): (onchain − fair) / fair × 100. Null unless both prices were read, and null on an unverified row (the figure is withheld; see rawGapPct). rawGapPct (number | null): The same gap before the plausibility check. Equal to gapPct on every row except an unverified one, where it keeps the figure that was withheld. Never chart, rank or alert on it. status (string): One of premium, discount, drifting, in-line, thin, unverified, no-pool, pool-unreadable, feed-unreadable. Rules in the methodology. trusted (boolean): Whether the tracker stands behind this row’s gap: true only for premium, discount, drifting and in-line rows whose pool read is fresh (not poolStale). Top movers and gap alerts use trusted rows only.

chunks.title: API reference
chunks.text: stands behind this row’s gap: true only for premium, discount, drifting and in-line rows whose pool read is fresh (not poolStale). Top movers and gap alerts use trusted rows only. untrustedReason (string | null): Why trusted is false, in a sentence, e.g. The pool holds $4,210, under the $10,000 needed to flag a gap. Null on a trusted row. onchainSource (string | null): chain when this cycle’s onchain price was read from the pool contract itself, api when it is DexScreener’s or GeckoTerminal’s reading (a venue the tracker cannot re-read on chain). Null when there is no onchain price. onchainAt (string | null): When that onchain price was read (ISO). For api prices this can be older than generatedAt. Null when there is no onchain price. pool (Pool | null): The pool used, below. poolError (string | null): Why pools could not be read, if they could not. logo (string | null): The stock’s logo: the token’s own where it carries the company mark, else the company’s own site icon. An absolute URL on gullylabs.xyz. chainLogo (string | null): The chain’s logo, an absolute URL on gullylabs.xyz. poolStale (boolean): True when the pool figures are the last good read rather than a fresh one. pool dex (string): The venue’s id, as DexScreener or GeckoTerminal names it. labels (string[]): Venue labels, e.g. v3. against (string): Symbol of the other token in the pool. url (string): The pool on DexScreener or GeckoTerminal. pair (string): Pool address. liquidityUsd (number): Liquidity of this pool. volume24hUsd (number): 24-hour volume of this pool. pools (number): How many pools with a price were found for the token. totalLiquidityUsd (number): Liquidity summed over those pools. totalVolume24hUsd (number): 24-hour volume summed over those pools.

chunks.title: API reference
chunks.text: One token’s gap history: a snapshot every five minutes. Seven days are open to everyone; paid plans keep more (see Plans & alerts). chain (string): Chain key, default robinhood. 2 to 12 lowercase letters. ticker (string, required): 1 to 8 letters or dots; case does not matter. days (integer, optional): Window in days, from 1 up to what your plan includes. Without it you get the last seven days, as before. Over your plan’s limit answers 403; past seven days the answer adds days and is not cached publicly. The answer is { chain, ticker, points }, where each point is a tuple [unixSeconds, gapPct, onchain, fair], oldest first. A chain or ticker the tracker does not know returns an empty points array, not an error.

chunks.title: API reference
chunks.text: Top movers: how each token’s gap to fair, and its onchain price, changed over the last hour or day, computed from the same five-minute snapshots as the history. For every token the latest snapshot is compared with the snapshot closest to one window earlier. Only tokens whose status is trusted right now (premium, discount, drifting or in-line) and that have both points are ranked; nothing is interpolated. window (string, optional): 24h (default) or 1h. limit (integer, optional): How many rows per ranking, 1 to 50, default 10. chain (string, optional): Rank one chain only, e.g. bsc. ticker (string, optional): With chain: also return that token’s own change in stock (null when it has none). Top level window (string): 1h or 24h. windowSeconds (number): 3600 or 86400. toleranceSeconds (number): How far the earlier snapshot may sit from exactly one window ago: 15 minutes for 1h, 2 hours for 24h. Further than that and the token is left out. asOf (string | null): The newest snapshot compared. Null when nothing could be compared. from, to (string | null): The comparison times: to is asOf, from one window earlier. Each row carries its own exact pair. eligible (number): Tokens with both points and a trusted status. left (object): Why the others are out: untrusted, noHistory, staleHistory (latest snapshot over 30 minutes old), tooShort. historyHours (number): How many hours the longest series covers.

chunks.title: API reference
chunks.text: and a trusted status. left (object): Why the others are out: untrusted, noHistory, staleHistory (latest snapshot over 30 minutes old), tooShort. historyHours (number): How many hours the longest series covers. note (string | null): Set when nothing could be ranked, e.g. Needs 24h of snapshots: the longest series so far covers 6.5 h. byGap (Mover[]): Largest absolute gap change first. byPrice (Mover[]): Largest absolute onchain price change first. stock (Mover | null): Only with chain and ticker. Mover chain, ticker, name, token (string): As in the tracker rows. status, gapPct, onchain, fair (see Rows): The token’s current status and prices, as in /api/tracker. liquidityUsd (number | null): Liquidity of the pool its price comes from. gapThen, gapNow (number): Gap % in the earlier and the latest snapshot. gapChangePp (number): gapNow − gapThen, in percentage points. onchainThen, onchainNow (number): Onchain price in the two snapshots. priceChangePct (number | null): Onchain price change in %. from, to (string): Times of the two snapshots compared. spark ([unixSeconds, gapPct][]): The gap over the window, at most 48 points, for a sparkline.

chunks.title: API reference
chunks.text: /api/tracker (public, max-age=30, s-maxage=60, stale-while-revalidate=300): The data itself refreshes about every two minutes. /api/tracker/history (public, max-age=60, s-maxage=120, stale-while-revalidate=600): A new point is added every five minutes. /api/tracker/movers (public, max-age=30, s-maxage=60, stale-while-revalidate=300): Computed at most once a minute per window. Counted by the same rate limit. Answers are cacheable at the edge, so polling more than once a minute gains nothing. A sensible client polls every one to two minutes and keeps its last good answer when a request fails.

chunks.title: API reference
chunks.text: Anonymous requests are limited to 60 a minute per IP address. Requests that carry an API key in Authorization: Bearer <key> are counted against the key instead, at 600 a minute. Windows are fixed one-minute windows. An unknown or revoked key answers 401. Every response also states the limit in force, so a client can read it rather than hard-code it: X-RateLimit-Limit (success): Requests allowed per minute: 60 anonymous, 600 with a Free key, more on a paid plan. X-RateLimit-Remaining (success): Requests left in it. Retry-After (429): Seconds to wait before trying again. Need more? Get a free key, instantly. A key on a paid plan gets that plan’s higher limit; see Plans & alerts.

chunks.title: API reference
chunks.text: Errors are JSON with a single error string. 400 (history: chain or ticker malformed): Check the parameters. Body: {"error":"chain and ticker"}. 400 (movers: window, limit, chain or ticker malformed): Use window=1h or 24h, a limit from 1 to 50, and a ticker only with a chain. 405 (a method other than GET or OPTIONS): Use GET. 401 (unknown or revoked API key): Check the key, or request one at developers.gullylabs.xyz. 403 (history: days beyond what your plan includes): Ask for fewer days, or move to a plan with more history. The body names your limit in historyDays. 429 (rate limit exceeded): Wait for Retry-After seconds, or use an API key. 502 (the tracker could not be built at all): Retry in a minute. A partial failure is not a 502: it shows as unreadable rows.

chunks.title: Widget guide
chunks.text: Live tracker data on any page, from one script tag and one element. No build step, no dependencies, no key. Embed the Gully Labs stock token tracker on any page: a live ticker, a one-stock badge or a table of the widest gaps. Every option, theming, behaviour and the CSP it needs.

chunks.title: Widget guide
chunks.text: Add an element where the widget should appear, and the script once per page: Prefer to click? The widget builder sets every option with a live preview and writes the snippet for you.

chunks.title: Widget guide
chunks.text: Every option is a data attribute on the element. All but the type are optional. data-gully-widget (ticker | badge | table): Which widget. Anything else draws a ticker. data-chain (all | robinhood | bsc): Which chain’s stocks. Default all. On a badge it picks the chain when a ticker exists on both. data-ticker (e.g. NVDA): Badge only, required: the stock to show. data-theme (dark | light): Default dark. data-limit (number, 1 to 60): Ticker: how many stocks in the strip (default every stock). Table: how many rows (default 5). data-api (URL): API base. Default https://gullylabs.xyz. Only needed for testing against another deployment.

chunks.title: Widget guide
chunks.text: A smooth scrolling strip of every stock with a readable gap: ticker, onchain price, gap to fair. It pauses while the pointer is over it or it has keyboard focus.

chunks.title: Widget guide
chunks.text: One stock: its ticker, onchain price and gap to fair, with the fair price and its source underneath. A thin pool or a closed market is said so in the caption.

chunks.title: Widget guide
chunks.text: The widest gaps, largest first, from pools deep enough to trust (thin pools are left out). With data-chain="all" each row names its chain.

chunks.title: Widget guide
chunks.text: Two themes, dark and light. Gaps outside the in-line band are teal above fair and vermilion below; in-line gaps and thin pools stay neutral. Ticker and table fill the width of their element; a badge is at most 340 px wide. Size the element to size the widget. Below 360 px the table drops its fair column so nothing is cut off. The widget draws inside its own shadow root, so your CSS does not reach in and its CSS does not leak out. The outer box is exposed as a part: [data-gully-widget]::part(widget) can set its border radius or shadow.

chunks.title: Widget guide
chunks.text: One request to the API per page, however many widgets share it, repeated every 60 seconds. If a refresh fails, the last good figures stay on screen and the footer reads “last read” instead of “live”. Before the first answer the widget says it is reading; if that fails, it says so and retries every minute. Errors stay inside the widget. Nothing is thrown into your page. Widgets added after the page loads, for example by a single-page app, are picked up automatically. window.GullyWidget.scan() forces a scan. Under prefers-reduced-motion the ticker stops scrolling and becomes a strip you can scroll by hand. Every widget carries a small “Gully Labs tracker” link to the live tracker. It is part of the free embed and stays. The widget never sends an API key and should not: anything in a page’s HTML is public. Its requests are anonymous and edge-cached. For heavier use, call the API from your server with a key.

chunks.title: Widget guide
chunks.text: If your site sends a Content Security Policy, allow the script and its one API origin: Add these to the directives you already have. The widget styles itself with a constructed stylesheet, so it needs no style-src 'unsafe-inline' in browsers that support them; older browsers fall back to a <style> element inside the shadow root. Subresource integrity widget.js is updated in place at the same address, so an integrity hash would break on the next release. Use the CSP above instead.

chunks.title: SDK
chunks.text: Two small MIT packages: a typed client for the tracker API, and the widget with a loader and a React component. Both are optional; the API and the widget work without them. The Gully Labs SDK: a typed TypeScript client for the stock token tracker API, and the embeddable widget with a React component.

chunks.title: SDK
chunks.text: @gullylabs/tracker: a typed client with no dependencies. Runs in browsers, Node 18+, Bun, Deno and edge runtimes. @gullylabs/widget: loads widget.js once and mounts widgets, with @gullylabs/widget/react for React. Source: github.com/gully-labs/sdk.

chunks.title: SDK
chunks.text: Rows are the same objects the API reference describes. A price that cannot be read is null, never zero; isTrusted(row) keeps the rows the tracker itself would chart. tracker.rateLimit holds the limit the last response reported.

chunks.title: SDK
chunks.text: Every option of the widget guide is a prop. To self-host the script, copy @gullylabs/widget/widget.js to your site and pass its URL as scriptSrc.

chunks.title: SDK
chunks.text: Anonymous calls get 60 a minute per IP. A key from the developer portal raises it to 600. The tracker refreshes every minute, so polling faster returns the same data.

chunks.title: API keys
chunks.text: The API is open without a key. A key raises your rate limit and counts your requests against your own allowance instead of your IP address. When you need a Gully Labs API key, how to get one instantly by signing in with a wallet, how to send it as a Bearer token, and how rate limits are reported.

chunks.title: API keys
chunks.text: Not for the widget: it is anonymous and shares one cached request per page. Not for trying the API, or for a page that reads it once a minute. Yes for a backend, bot or app that calls the API often, or from shared infrastructure where many callers share one IP address.

chunks.title: API keys
chunks.text: Keys are free and issued instantly at developers.gullylabs.xyz. There is no form and no approval: Press Connect wallet and pick any browser wallet or Coinbase Wallet. Your wallet address is your account; there is no email or password. Sign the message your wallet shows. It is Sign-In with Ethereum (EIP-4361): a signature, not a transaction, so it costs nothing and moves nothing. It names developers.gullylabs.xyz, expires after ten minutes and can be used once. Open API keys, press Create key and name it. The key works at once. Copy it then: it is shown in full only once, because we store only a hash of it. Smart-contract wallets (EIP-1271, including ones not deployed yet, ERC-6492) are accepted on Ethereum, Base, BNB Chain and Robinhood Chain. A sign-in lasts 30 days on that browser.

chunks.title: API keys
chunks.text: A wallet can hold up to five live keys. Each has its own 600-a-minute allowance. Rotate gives a key a new secret and stops the old one immediately; its name and usage history stay. Revoke stops a key for good. The dashboard shows requests per hour or day for each key, the error rate, and the last 50 requests with status and latency. Answers served from the edge cache never reach our servers and are not counted. A key issued through the earlier request form keeps working. Link it to your wallet from the API keys page to manage it there.

chunks.title: API keys
chunks.text: Send it in the Authorization header as a Bearer token, on either endpoint:

chunks.title: API keys
chunks.text: Every successful response carries X-RateLimit-Limit and X-RateLimit-Remaining. Past the limit the API answers 429 with a Retry-After header in seconds. Today that is 60 requests a minute per IP address without a key and 600 a minute with one; read the headers rather than hard-coding either, because they can change. Details in the API reference. The data refreshes about every two minutes, so polling more often than once a minute returns the same answer.

chunks.title: API keys
chunks.text: Keep the key on a server or in an environment variable. Anything shipped to a browser, an app bundle or a public repository is public. Do not put a key in the widget snippet: the widget does not read one. If a key is exposed, rotate or revoke it on the developers dashboard; the old secret stops working at once. To serve many browser users, call the API from your server with your key and cache the answer for a minute. Your users then never touch the limit.

chunks.title: Plans & alerts
chunks.text: The API stays free. Paid plans raise the per-key rate limit, add gap alerts and keep a longer history. You pay in ETH, BNB, USDC or USDT from your own wallet straight to ours. Paid plans for the Gully Labs tracker API, paid in ETH, BNB, USDC or USDT on Base, Ethereum, BNB Chain or Arbitrum with no custody; gap alerts by webhook or Telegram; the webhook payload and how to verify its signature.

chunks.title: Plans & alerts
chunks.text: A plan belongs to your wallet account and applies to every key it holds. The limits below are read live from GET /api/plans, the same source the pricing page and the dashboard use.

chunks.title: Plans & alerts
chunks.text: Prices are in US dollars. You pay in ETH, BNB, USDC or USDT on Base, Ethereum, BNB Chain or Arbitrum, straight to the Gully Labs treasury wallet, which is the same address on every chain. Open Plan & billing on the developer dashboard, choose a plan, then a chain and an asset. You get a quote: the exact amount to send and the treasury address, valid for 20 minutes. Stablecoins count one to one with the dollar; the quote adds a few millionths as a tag. ETH and BNB are priced by the Chainlink USD feed on the same chain at the moment of the quote and rounded up, with a unique tail in the last digits. The quote shows the feed, its round and when it last updated. If the feed is more than two hours old, no quote is given in that coin. Press Pay with a wallet for a one-click transfer (the wallet is asked to switch to the quote’s chain), or send the amount from any wallet or exchange and paste the transaction hash. The server reads the receipt and the transaction from a public node of that chain and checks that they agree. A payment counts when it succeeded, is on the quote’s chain, paid the treasury in the quoted asset, has the confirmations above, and its hash was never used before on any chain. The plan starts the moment it is confirmed.

chunks.title: Plans & alerts
chunks.text: chain, paid the treasury in the quoted asset, has the confirmations above, and its hash was never used before on any chain. The plan starts the moment it is confirmed. From the wallet you signed in with, at least the price counts: any stablecoin amount from the dollar price up, or at least the quoted amount of ETH or BNB (paying more is accepted, paying less is refused and says by how much). From any other wallet or an exchange, send the exact quoted amount: its last digits tag the payment as yours, so nobody watching the treasury can claim it. A coin payment must be mined while its quote holds (ten minutes of grace). A payment buys days. Paying again for the same plan adds them to the end; a different plan starts that day. Nothing renews by itself: to cancel, don’t pay again. When a plan lapses you are back on Free and your keys keep working at the Free limit. The payment goes straight to the treasury wallet in your own transfer. We hold no balance and no card, and nothing leaves your wallet unless you sign it. Other Gully Labs work (Chain Kit, Gully Analytics, services) is billed with an invoice link of the form gullylabs.xyz/pay/…. It takes the same assets and checks; since nobody signs in there, a payment matches an invoice only by the exact quoted amount. Once paid, the page links the transaction and a printable receipt.

chunks.title: Plans & alerts
chunks.text: GET /api/tracker/history takes days, up to what your plan includes. Without it the answer is the last seven days, unchanged. Asking for more than your plan includes answers 403 with your limit in historyDays. History is what the tracker recorded since long-term storage began; days before that are simply absent, never filled in.

chunks.title: Plans & alerts
chunks.text: An alert watches one stock (chain and ticker) or every stock the tracker follows, for one condition: gap ({ type: "gap", pct }): The gap between on-chain and fair price is at least pct percent, above or below. status ({ type: "status", status }): The tracker flags the stock premium, discount, or either. Alerts are checked on every tracker snapshot, every five minutes. Per stock, an alert fires when its condition becomes true and re-arms once it is false again. It does not repeat while the condition simply stays true. Each alert sends at most one delivery every 30 minutes. Stocks that trigger during that pause go out with the next delivery if their condition still holds. Only rows the tracker would itself flag count: a readable feed and pool, a pool deep enough to flag, a fresh pool read and an open feed session. Anything else neither fires nor re-arms. Each delivery is logged in the dashboard with its HTTP status (the last 50 per alert). Use Test to send an alert.test delivery with no events. When a plan lapses, the alerts beyond the Free allowance stay listed but are paused until you delete some or upgrade; the oldest ones keep running.

chunks.title: Plans & alerts
chunks.text: A second kind of alert watches DeepCore, the launchpad and DEX in the Gully Labs family, for new token launches. It has no stock: it watches one DeepCore chain, or every chain when chainId is left empty. deepcore-launch ({ type: "deepcore-launch", chainId }): A token launches on DeepCore on that chain: 56 BNB Chain, 999 HyperEVM, 4663 Robinhood Chain or 8453 Base; null for any of them. DeepCore’s public API (GET /v1/launches) is read every 90 seconds. Each launch fires once, the first time it is seen; after a restart nothing already seen is sent again. Only launches made after the alert was created count (with an hour of slack for indexer lag), so a new alert does not replay the backlog. One delivery at most every 5 minutes per alert: launches seen in the meantime wait and go out together, up to the 20 most recent. A paused, muted or over-the-plan alert neither sends nor queues: launches it missed are not sent later. It counts against your plan’s alerts like a gap alert, and delivers the same way: webhook, Telegram or both, signed the same way (see below). When DeepCore cannot be read, nothing fires and nothing is invented; the next good read catches up on launches it has not seen.

chunks.title: Plans & alerts
chunks.text: both, signed the same way (see below). When DeepCore cannot be read, nothing fires and nothing is invented; the next good read catches up on launches it has not seen. In Telegram, anyone can ask the bot /launches for the five latest DeepCore launches on every chain, or /launches base (also bsc, robinhood, hyperevm, or a chain id) for one chain. It reads the same 90-second cache as the alerts, says when the list is older because DeepCore could not be read, and names any chain DeepCore itself could not read. Launch information is not advice.

chunks.title: Plans & alerts
chunks.text: We POST JSON with these headers: Content-Type: application/json, X-Gully-Timestamp (Unix seconds) and X-Gully-Signature (sha256= and the hex HMAC). Answer with any 2xx within 5 seconds; we do not follow redirects and do not retry, and the status is shown in your delivery log.

chunks.title: Plans & alerts
chunks.text: The signature is HMAC-SHA256 with the alert’s secret over `${timestamp}.${rawBody}`. The secret (whsec_…) is shown once when you create the alert; New secret replaces it. Compare in constant time and refuse old timestamps. Webhook URLs must be https:// on a public address. The host is resolved before every delivery and private, loopback, link-local and other reserved addresses are refused. See API keys for keeping secrets out of browser code; the same applies here.

chunks.title: Plans & alerts
chunks.text: An alert can message a Telegram chat as well as, or instead of, calling a webhook. In the Alerts tab of the dashboard press Connect Telegram: it opens the bot with a one-time code (ten minutes, single use) that links the chat to your wallet account, so there is no chat id to copy. Add to a group does the same for a group; only the person who linked a group can unlink it. Then tick Telegram on any alert. Each message names the stock and chain, the gap, the on-chain and fair prices, the status and the pool liquidity, with a link to the stock page. Open NVDA opens the stock page; Mute 24h pauses that alert, on every channel, for 24 hours. Resume in the dashboard ends a mute early. Deliveries appear in the alert's log like webhook ones, with the result Telegram gave. In the chat, /alerts lists your alerts and /stop unlinks. Anyone can ask the bot /gap NVDA (or /gap NVDA bsc) and /top for the five widest trusted gaps. A figure the tracker could not read is said to be unreadable, never shown as zero. Which channels the server offers is public at GET /api/alerts/channels.

chunks.title: Teams & workspaces
chunks.text: Every wallet account is a workspace. Invite teammates by wallet or by link, give each a role, and see who changed what. Share one Gully Labs developer account with a team: workspaces, roles and what each may change, invites by wallet or by link, the activity log and CSV exports of usage and payments.

chunks.title: Teams & workspaces
chunks.text: When a wallet first signs in to the developer portal, it gets its own workspace and is its owner. Everything in the portal belongs to the workspace: API keys, gap and DeepCore launch alerts, the linked Telegram chat, Gully Analytics, the plan and its payments. Members share all of it; nothing is copied per person. The workspace is named after its owner (0x1234…abcd’s workspace) until an admin or the owner renames it. A workspace holds at most 25 people, the owner included, and 20 open invites at a time. Membership is checked on every request. A member who is removed is moved back to their own workspace on their next request. If the owner’s wallet is blocked, the workspace is unavailable to every member.

chunks.title: Teams & workspaces
chunks.text: Every member can see everything in the workspace. A role decides what they may change: owner (everything): The wallet that owns the workspace. Cannot be removed or demoted, and is the only one who can add, change or remove admins. admin (keys, alerts, Telegram, Gully Analytics, billing, company details, the team): Invites and manages developers, billing members and viewers, and renames the workspace. developer (keys, alerts, Telegram, Gully Analytics): Creates, renames, rotates and revokes keys; manages alerts and analytics websites; can open Gully Analytics in one click (see single sign-on). Cannot pay or manage the team. billing (billing, company details): Buys and renews plans (tracker API and Gully Analytics) and keeps the invoice details current. viewer (nothing): Read-only: keys (prefixes only), usage, alerts, billing and the activity log. Your own profile, your sign-in sessions, switching workspace, leaving one and accepting an invite are open to every role. A request beyond your role answers 403 with {"code":"forbidden-role"}.

chunks.title: Teams & workspaces
chunks.text: Owners and admins invite from the Team tab, in two ways: By wallet. Enter the teammate’s address. The invite waits for that wallet: they sign in to the portal and accept it there. Nobody else can use it. By link. The portal makes a link (https://developers.gullylabs.xyz/#invite=…) that anyone who signs in with a wallet can accept, once. The link is shown once; only a hash of it is kept, so it cannot be shown again. Send it privately. Every invite carries the role it grants and expires after 7 days. Accepted, revoked and expired invites stop working at once. Open invites can be revoked from the Team tab. Only the owner can invite, or revoke the invite of, an admin. Opening a link shows the workspace name, the role and who invited you before you accept. Unknown links and repeated attempts are rate limited per address. Owners and admins change a member’s role or remove them from the Team tab. Removing someone moves their sessions back to their own workspace, which is untouched.

chunks.title: Teams & workspaces
chunks.text: If you belong to more than one workspace, the portal’s workspace switcher lists yours first, then the others by name. The choice is kept for that sign-in session only, so two browsers can work in two workspaces. Members can leave a workspace from the Team tab; the owner cannot leave their own.

chunks.title: Teams & workspaces
chunks.text: The Activity tab lists who did what in the workspace, newest first, 50 at a time. It records: Keys: key.created, key.renamed, key.rotated, key.revoked, key.linked. Alerts and Telegram: alert.created, alert.updated, alert.tested, alert.deleted, telegram.linked, telegram.unlinked. Billing and analytics: billing.quote, billing.paid, analytics.trial, analytics.site_added, analytics.site_removed, analytics.password_reset, analytics.quote, analytics.plan. Team and account: team.invited, team.invite_revoked, team.joined, team.role_changed, team.removed, team.left, workspace.renamed, company.updated, profile.updated, sessions.revoked. Usage: usage.threshold, by system, when the workspace’s busiest key passes 80% or 100% of the plan’s per-minute limit (at most once a day per threshold). The owner can also have it sent to Telegram from their profile. Only successful changes are logged, and never a secret. A workspace keeps its newest 1,000 events and nothing older than 180 days. Reading it from code Page backwards by passing the previous page’s nextCursor as ?cursor=. A cursor that has aged out answers 400: start again from the first page.

chunks.title: Teams & workspaces
chunks.text: Two downloads from the portal, for whatever workspace is active. Any member, viewers included, can download them. usage.csv (one per time bucket and key): Requests made with the workspace’s keys: hourly buckets for 24h and 7d, daily (UTC) for 30d. client_err is 4xx other than 429, limited is 429, server_err is 5xx. payments.csv (one per payment, oldest first): Every payment for the workspace’s plans (tracker API and Gully Analytics), with the asset, chain, transaction hash and an explorer link. Every text cell that starts with =, +, -, @, a tab or a carriage return gets a leading ', so a spreadsheet shows it as text instead of running it as a formula. Cells with commas, quotes or line breaks are quoted. Files are UTF-8 with CRLF line ends.

chunks.title: Gully Analytics
chunks.text: Privacy-friendly web analytics with Web3 tracking for dapps: page views plus wallet connects, chain switches and transactions. It is a fork of Umami; everything Umami does still works. Gully Analytics: sign up with a wallet, install the tracker, Web3 events, address privacy modes, plans and what happens at the quota or when a plan lapses.

chunks.title: Gully Analytics
chunks.text: Open the developer portal, connect a wallet and sign the sign-in message (no transaction, no gas). In the Analytics tab press Start free trial. The server creates a Gully Analytics login for your wallet and shows its password once; copy it. We do not keep the password. Reset password in the same tab sets a new one and signs out open sessions. Add a website with its name and domain. The tab shows its website id, the install snippet, a link to its dashboard and the events counted this month. The free trial runs once per wallet. After it, choose a plan in the same tab to keep recording.

chunks.title: Gully Analytics
chunks.text: The quickest way in is Open Gully Analytics in the Analytics tab of the developer portal. It signs you straight in to the dashboard, with no password to type: the portal asks the server for a one-time sign-in link (POST /api/developer/analytics/sso), and the browser opens it on analytics.gullylabs.xyz. The link works once and only for 60 seconds, from the browser that asked for it. Only a hash of it is kept. Owners, admins and developers of the workspace can use it; billing members and viewers cannot. Everyone in the workspace opens the same Gully Analytics account. It never shows, changes or resets the account’s password, so a password you saved keeps working. The password login at analytics.gullylabs.xyz/login still works for anyone with the password. Forgot it? Reset password in the portal’s Analytics tab sets a new one.

chunks.title: Gully Analytics
chunks.text: Put the snippet on every page, before the closing head tag. The Analytics tab gives it with your website id filled in. Without data-web3="true" the script behaves exactly like the Umami tracker. The usual Umami attributes (data-domains, data-do-not-track, data-tag, data-before-send, …) still apply, and Web3 events respect them.

chunks.title: Gully Analytics
chunks.text: The script finds wallets through EIP-6963 and window.ethereum and watches what your dapp asks of them. It never calls a wallet method itself, so it cannot trigger a wallet prompt. All four events are standard custom events with event data, so they also show under Events, Goals, Funnels and filters. chainId is a decimal number; wallet is the wallet’s EIP-6963 id (io.metamask, io.rabby, …) or its name. You can send these events yourself too, and the Web3 dashboard reads them the same:

chunks.title: Gully Analytics
chunks.text: data-web3-address decides what is stored about the wallet address: hash (default) (counted): The first 16 hex characters of the SHA-256 of the lowercase address. Wallets can be counted; the address cannot be read back. full (counted): The lowercase address. none (not counted): Nothing. Unique wallets and transactions per wallet show 0 or a dash. Hashing needs a secure context (HTTPS or localhost); on plain HTTP the address is dropped rather than sent in clear. A hash of a public address is pseudonymous, not anonymous: anyone with a candidate address can hash it and compare. Use none if that matters for your users.

chunks.title: Gully Analytics
chunks.text: The plans below are read live from GET /api/plans (field analytics), the same source the pricing page and the dashboard use. An event is any call the tracker makes for one of your websites: page views, custom events and Web3 events. They are counted across your websites per calendar month in UTC. At the limit, new events are not recorded until the month turns or you upgrade. The tracker gets an HTTP 402 answer and stops sending for the rest of that page view. Websites beyond what your plan includes (after a downgrade, say) do not record until you remove some or upgrade; the oldest ones keep recording. Paying works like the tracker API plans (see Paying): ETH, BNB, USDC or USDT on Base, Ethereum, BNB Chain or Arbitrum, straight to the treasury, checked on chain. A payment buys days; paying again for the same plan adds them to the end. Nothing renews by itself. When a trial or plan ends, recording stops. Your dashboard stays readable for days; after that the account and its data may be deleted.

chunks.title: Gully Analytics
chunks.text: Sign in at analytics.gullylabs.xyz with the login from the Analytics tab. Each website has the usual Umami views plus a Web3 tab: unique wallets, connects, connect rate, transactions, transactions per wallet, a visit → connect → transaction funnel, chains, wallet apps and the top pages by connects. The Umami REST API works with your own login: sign in with POST /api/auth/login and send the token as Authorization: Bearer …. The Web3 figures are at GET /api/websites/{websiteId}/web3?startAt=…&endAt=…. The source is public: gully-labs/umami, MIT licensed like Umami.

chunks.title: Gully Pay
chunks.text: Non-custodial crypto billing: every payment is a plain transfer from the payer’s wallet straight to the treasury, read back from the chain. Invoices, reusable pay links, a hosted checkout and signed webhooks. Gully Pay: invoices and reusable pay links in ETH, BNB, USDC or USDT on four chains, wallet QR codes, the Pay with crypto button, and signed merchant webhooks with how to verify them.

chunks.title: Gully Pay
chunks.text: An invoice (/pay/inv_…) asks for one US dollar amount. The payer picks a chain and an asset and gets a quote: the exact amount to send, valid for 20 minutes. Stablecoins count one to one with a unique tag in the last digits; ETH and BNB are priced by the Chainlink USD feed on the same chain. A payment is checked on chain (success, right chain, right asset, the treasury, the exact amount, enough confirmations, never used before) before the invoice is marked paid. The same rules as API plans apply. Base (8453) (10): USDC (6 decimals), ETH Ethereum (1) (6): USDC, USDT (6 decimals), ETH BNB Chain (56) (15): USDT, USDC (18 decimals), BNB Arbitrum (42161) (10): USDC (6 decimals), ETH The live list, read from GET /api/plans as you look at this page (hover a chain for its assets and confirmations): Nothing is held in between: the transfer goes to the treasury in the payer’s own transaction. If no treasury is configured, every page says checkout is closed and shows no amount or QR.

chunks.title: Gully Pay
chunks.text: A pay link (/pay/l/pl_…, an unguessable id) is reusable: every payer who opens it gets an invoice of their own, linked back to the link, then lands in the checkout. Links are made in the admin dashboard. title, description (string): Shown on the link, the checkout and the receipt. amount (fixed | open): A fixed USD amount, or open: the payer types an amount between a minimum and a maximum. The server checks it; the page cannot change it. assets (string[]): Which chain and asset pairs it takes (all by default). active (boolean): Switched off links take no payments. expiresAt (date | null): After it, the link takes no payments. maxUses (number | null): How many paid uses it allows. Checkouts in progress count against it, so a one-off link cannot be paid twice. webhook (https URL | null): Where its events go (webhooks). An invoice made from a link stays open for an hour. Its quote holds 20 minutes and can be renewed. Each address may start ten checkouts from links an hour. A switched-off, expired or used-up link says so plainly and starts no checkout.

chunks.title: Gully Pay
chunks.text: Title, amount and a status pill: awaiting payment, confirming, paid, expired or cancelled. Assets grouped by chain; the exact amount, large; a wallet QR; copy buttons for the amount, the treasury address and the token contract. A countdown on the quote, and a new quote when it runs out. A payment sent in time can still be checked after. Pay with wallet sends the exact transfer from a connected wallet. Or send from anywhere and paste the transaction hash. Live confirmations (n / needed), then a receipt with the explorer link, ready to print or save as PDF.

chunks.title: Gully Pay
chunks.text: Every quote carries an uri: an EIP-681 payment request for the exact amount, built on the server from base units (never floating point). The QR encodes it. Wallet support for EIP-681 varies: some read only the address, some ignore the amount or the chain. The checkout always shows the address, the exact amount and the token contract with copy buttons. Check the amount and the network in the wallet before sending.

chunks.title: Gully Pay
chunks.text: Paste this on any site to send buyers to a pay link or an invoice. The link alone opens the checkout in a new tab; the optional script opens it in a popup window. The admin shows the snippet for each link and invoice. The checkout cannot be put in an iframe: its pages send frame-ancestors limited to Gully Labs itself, so wallet prompts and the address bar stay visible to the payer.

chunks.title: Gully Pay
chunks.text: A pay link, an invoice, or a default endpoint for everything else can have a webhook. When an invoice has its own, or its link has one, events go there; otherwise to the default, if set. invoice.paid (The payment is confirmed and the invoice marked paid.): invoice, link, payment invoice.expired (An open invoice ran out without a payment.): invoice, link invoice.cancelled (Gully Labs cancelled the invoice; it can no longer be paid. A cancelled invoice never sends invoice.expired afterwards.): invoice, link webhook.test (The admin pressed Send test event.): target, message https only. No user name or password in the URL. The host must resolve only to public addresses: private, loopback, link-local and reserved ranges are refused, and the request goes to the address that was checked. The signing secret (whsec_…) is shown once, when the endpoint is set. Rotating it shows the new one once; the old one stops at once. Five-second timeout, redirects not followed, the response body is not read.

chunks.title: Gully Pay
chunks.text: Every request carries two headers. The signature is an HMAC-SHA256, with your secret, of the timestamp, a dot, and the raw body: X-Gully-Timestamp (unix seconds): When it was sent. Refuse old ones (five minutes) to stop replays. X-Gully-Signature (sha256=<hex>): hex(HMAC-SHA256(secret, `${timestamp}.${rawBody}`)) It is the same scheme as gap alerts, so one verifier serves both.

chunks.title: Gully Pay
chunks.text: The first attempt goes out at once. Any answer other than 2xx, a timeout or a network error is retried after 1, 5, 10, 20 and 30 minutes: six attempts over about an hour. Then the delivery is marked failed. Retries carry the same event id and body; each is signed again with the current secret and timestamp. The queue is stored on disk, so a restart loses nothing: attempts that came due while the server was down go out when it is back. Each link and invoice shows its delivery log in the admin: event, state, attempts, last answer. A finished delivery (failed or delivered) can be redelivered from the admin, for example after your endpoint was down for longer than the retries. The same event goes out again, with the same id and body, as a new delivery with its own six attempts. Your handler should already drop an id it has handled. Events may arrive out of order and, rarely, more than once. Treat invoice.paid as the source of truth for a sale and look the invoice up by id.

chunks.title: Changelog
chunks.text: What changed, newest first. What changed in the Gully Labs tracker, its API, the widget and these docs.

chunks.title: Changelog

The public API: /api/tracker and /api/tracker/history. The embeddable widget (ticker, badge, table) and its builder. API keys for higher rate limits. These docs. chunks.title: Gully Analytics
chunks.text: Analytics that see the wallet. Page views alone don’t tell a dapp what worked. Gully Analytics adds what happens next: which visits connected a wallet, on which chain, with which wallet app, and which went on to send a transaction. Free trial. Built on Umami, MIT licensed. Our changes are MIT too. Start free trial Wallet connects. Detected through EIP-6963 and window.ethereum, by observing the wallet, never by prompting it. Chains and switches. Every connect, chain switch and transaction carries its chain, named for Ethereum, Base, BNB Chain, Robinhood Chain, Arc and more. Visit → wallet → transaction. A funnel from session to connected wallet to sent transaction, plus top pages by connects and wallet apps used. Addresses hashed by default. Unique wallets are counted from a one-way hash of the address. Full addresses or none are one attribute away. Everything Umami does. Page views, referrers, countries, devices, events and goals, cookie-free, on a dashboard you own. Opt-in, small, open. Web3 tracking turns on with one attribute; the whole script stays a few kilobytes. The source is public. Sign in and add your site. Connect a wallet in the developer portal, start the free trial and add your domain. Add the script. One tag on your dapp, with data-web3="true". Use your dapp as usual. Connects, chain switches and transactions are recorded as they happen. Read the Web3 tab. Wallets, connect rate, transactions, chains and the funnel for any date range. Gully Analytics. Privacy-friendly web analytics for dapps: page views plus wallet connects, chains and transactions, with a visit to wallet to transaction funnel.

chunks.title: Chain Kit
chunks.text: An explorer for your chain. A new chain needs a block explorer on day one. Chain Kit is Blockscout, the open-source explorer, set up for your chain, in your brand, and run by the team that builds on these chains every day. Available on request. Built on Blockscout, GPL-3.0. Our deployment layer is GPL-3.0 too. Talk to us about your chain Full explorer. Blocks, transactions, addresses, tokens, NFTs, contract verification, APIs and charts, from Blockscout. Your brand. Your name, logos, colours and links across the explorer, configured rather than forked, so upgrades stay simple. Rollups included. Profiles for Arbitrum Nitro and Orbit chains like Robinhood Chain, and for chains like Arc with a stablecoin as gas. Operated for you. Provisioning, TLS, backups, upgrades and monitoring, with a runbook for every common failure. Sized honestly. A busy rollup needs terabytes; a young chain needs far less. We size the server and the RPC to your chain before anything is promised. Open source. Everything we add is public and GPL-3.0 like Blockscout itself. You are never locked in. Tell us about your chain. Chain id, RPC, settlement layer and how much history you need. We size and deploy. A dedicated server, your branding and the indexer, on a domain of your choice. Launch and run. We keep it indexed, upgraded and backed up while you build the chain. Chain Kit. A branded Blockscout block explorer for your EVM chain, deployed and operated by Gully Labs.

chunks.text: Plans for the Gully Labs tracker API and for Gully Analytics, paid in ETH, BNB, USDC or USDT on Base, Ethereum, BNB Chain or Arbitrum, with no custody.

Gully Analytics starts with a free trial. You pay in ETH, BNB, USDC or USDT from your own wallet, straight to ours: no card, no custody, nothing that renews behind your back.

chunks.title: API pricing
chunks.text: Paid in ETH, BNB, USDC or USDT on four chains, checked on chain, no custody. Plans & alerts docs

chunks.title: API pricing
chunks.text: Q: How do I pay? A: In ETH, BNB, USDC or USDT on (live value). Pick a plan in the developer dashboard, then a chain and an asset; it gives a quote with the exact amount and the Gully Labs treasury address, valid for 20 minutes. Pay with one click from a connected wallet, or send it from any wallet or exchange and paste the transaction hash. Q: What do I pay in? A: Prices are in US dollars. (live value) Stablecoins are counted one to one with the dollar. ETH and BNB are priced by the Chainlink USD feed on the same chain when you ask for the quote, rounded up; if that feed has not updated for two hours, no quote is given in that coin. Q: Do you hold my funds? A: No. Your coin or stablecoin goes straight to the Gully Labs treasury wallet in one transfer, the same as paying any address. There is no deposit, balance or card on file, and nothing is ever taken from your wallet without you signing it. Q: How is a payment checked? A: The server reads the transaction from a public node of its chain: it must have succeeded, paid the treasury at least the plan’s price in the quoted asset, and have enough blocks on top ((live value)). Each transaction counts once, on any chain. The plan starts the moment it is confirmed.

chunks.title: API pricing
chunks.text: the plan’s price in the quoted asset, and have enough blocks on top ((live value)). Each transaction counts once, on any chain. The plan starts the moment it is confirmed. Q: How do I cancel? A: Just don’t renew. A payment buys (live value) days and nothing renews by itself; when the days run out the account returns to Free with its keys still working at the Free limit. Q: Can I extend or switch? A: Paying again for the same plan adds days to the end of the current period. A different plan starts the day you pay for it; the days left on the old one are not carried over. Q: When does Gully Analytics stop recording? A: At the monthly event limit of your plan, until the month turns (UTC) or you upgrade; and when a trial or plan ends without being extended. Your dashboard stays readable for (live value) days after a plan ends; after that the account may be deleted. Plans are bought in the Analytics tab of the developer dashboard. Q: Can alerts come to Telegram? Q: What does Free include? A: Keys, usage charts and the request log, as today, with the limits shown above. Calling the API without any key keeps working too, at the anonymous limit.
